flashcard_questions.q: Which region of the brain is responsible for consciousness, intelligence, memory and language?
Which region of the brain coordinates muscular activity, balance and posture?
Which region of the brain controls unconscious activities such as breathing and heart rate?
Which part of the eye does most of the focusing as light enters?
What is the function of the iris in the eye?
flashcard_questions.a: It contains muscles that change the size of the pupil, controlling how much light enters.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the function of the retina at the back of the eye?
flashcard_questions.a: It converts the focused light into electrical impulses using its receptor cells.

flashcard_questions.q: To focus on a near object: ciliary muscles ____ → suspensory ligaments go ____ → lens becomes fat
To focus on a distant object: ciliary muscles ____ → suspensory ligaments pull ____ → lens becomes thin
What core temperature does the human body maintain?
Why must core body temperature stay close to 37 °C?
flashcard_questions.a: It is the optimum temperature for enzymes, which denature if the body gets too hot.

flashcard_questions.q: Which part of the brain acts as the thermoregulatory centre?
What is vasodilation when the body is too hot?
flashcard_questions.a: Blood vessels near the skin surface widen, so more thermal energy is lost by radiation.

flashcard_questions.q: What is vasoconstriction when the body is too cold?
flashcard_questions.a: Blood vessels near the skin surface narrow, so less thermal energy is lost to the surroundings.

flashcard_questions.q: How does sweating cool the body down?
flashcard_questions.a: As the water in sweat evaporates it absorbs thermal energy from the skin.

flashcard_questions.q: How does shivering warm the body up?
flashcard_questions.a: Rapid muscle contraction needs energy from respiration, which releases thermal energy as a by-product.
